edges.notes: Linux: namespaces, cgroups, overlayfs stack per Engine docs; Windows/macOS use different isolation stacks.
docker.service commonly systemd-managed on Linux.
Engine host services and some container images express supervision via unit files when systemd is PID 1.
Ecosystem overlap via CRI-compatible runtimes; clusters often use containerd rather than dockerd directly.
Modern Docker Engine uses containerd as lower-level runtime component per Engine architecture docs.
Engine builds, stores, and runs OCI-compatible images; format is standardized in OCI Image Spec (separate from Moby/dockerd).
docker push/pull and registry clients use HTTP APIs aligned with OCI distribution / Docker Registry V2 class semantics.
Executed containers are OCI runtime bundles; low-level runtimes implement the OCI Runtime Spec.
Linux Engine deployments can configure runsc where supported; Docker remains the engine, gVisor is an optional low-level runtime (survey-level).
Docker Engine uses BuildKit as the default `docker build` backend in modern releases; shared Moby/BuildKit ecosystem.
Developer workflows often build images with Docker and deploy workloads with Helm charts (survey-level).
Amazon ECS developer guide names Docker among integrated third-party tools.
Azure Container Apps overview documents pulling images from registries including Docker Hub.
Azure Container Instances overview documents Linux/Windows images from Docker Hub and other registries.
Many pulled OCI images (e.g. Alpine-class bases) ship musl-linked userlands; Docker runs them like other Linux images.
OCI/container images vs systemd portable OS-tree bundles address overlapping 'ship a service' goals with different formats.
Container images vs systemd sysext host /usr merge address overlapping delivery goals with different isolation models.
Container-delivered configuration vs host confext /etc merge address overlapping goals with different models.
Official and community images commonly use Alpine as a minimal musl-based Linux base; Docker pulls and runs them like other OCI images.
Official debian and debian:slim images are common glibc-based OCI bases; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
Official ubuntu images are common glibc-based OCI bases; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
Official fedora images are common glibc-based OCI bases; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
RHEL and UBI-class images are common glibc-based OCI bases where vendors publish them; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
Official rockylinux images are common glibc-based OCI bases; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
Official almalinux images are common glibc-based OCI bases; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
Official CentOS Stream OCI images are common glibc-based bases; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
Legacy centos:* OCI images were common glibc-based bases; Docker pulls may still reference historical tags where published.
Docker’s Linux bridge/NAT modes commonly install iptables/nftables rules backed by netfilter in typical deployments.
Docker’s default Linux containers use namespaces/cgroups; KVM is a different virtualization mechanism for VM-class isolation.
